# `cfr_sections`

**Code of Federal Regulations sections**

One row per GovInfo annual CFR granule, including sections, appendices, tables of contents and other structural units; metadata only, no regulatory body text. Neither a granule id nor a printed section number establishes the enclosing part, so each section granule is placed under the PART heading of its package's annual volume XML: Title 43 numbers sections by subpart (§ 1601.0-1 is in Part 1600), Title 41's parts contain a hyphen (`50-201`) and Title 14 Part 241 prints `19-8.1`. `part` is that structure; `cfr_ref` is the printed citation that joins the Federal Register side. Other granules keep the part their identifier spells, except in Title 41, whose identifiers cut a compound part at the hyphen (`…-part60` is Part 60-1): there a structural row takes the compound part its part granule's heading states (`60-2`), as the section rows do, and a Reserved part granule whose heading states no number takes NULL. The Parquet footer key `spicy_regs.cfr_sections.placement` records that every section row was placed by this rule; generations without it keep identifier-derived parts. The key says nothing of Title 41's structural rows, which no volume scan places: they take their compound part from their part granule's heading on every run from 2026-10-03, under the same key. A generation built before keeps the identifier's chapter there (`part` `60`, `cfr_ref` `41-60` on `…-part60-id334`), and `count(*) WHERE title = '41' AND section IS NULL AND part LIKE '%-%'` is 0 on it and above 0 once the compound parts are in. A package is re-placed only when it is new or its GovInfo lastModified changed; an unchanged package, or one whose volume cannot be read, keeps its prior rows. Missing credentials and incomplete source traversals refuse before output replacement. GovInfo's annual index package (`GPO-CFR-INDEX-2025`) is not a title volume and is not in the table. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

**Coverage.** Window. Annual-edition section metadata from the 2025 edition and, for some titles, the 2026 edition (`SELECT DISTINCT edition_year, title` lists which), not full publication history or body text. Each section's part comes from its volume's PART heading; on 2026-09-23 every compared Title 41, 43 and 14 section agreed with eCFR's 2025-01-01 structure. Receipts: fork-execution-2026-09-21/cfr-ancestry-fix-2026-09-23/ (candidate.json, validation.json). *(measured 2026-10-03)*

- **Parquet file:** `cfr_sections.parquet`
- **MCP `query_sql` support:** Configured; requires an available artifact.
- **Publication status:** Not established by this schema page or its measurement date.
- **Row count:** Not stated here; the MCP `describe_table` reply gives the live count under `publication`.

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `granule_id` | `VARCHAR` | GovInfo granule identifier. Primary key / dedup key, including non-section structural units. |
| `package_id` | `VARCHAR` | GovInfo package identifier for the enclosing annual CFR title and volume. |
| `cfr_ref` | `VARCHAR` | Join key to Federal Register `cfr_references_json`. For a section, the title and its printed citation (e.g. `43-1601.0-1`, `41-50-201.1`); Title 43 keeps its subpart-numbered spelling while `part` names the enclosing part. The Federal Register side cuts every Title 41 compound part at the hyphen (`41 CFR 60-1.4` reads `41-60`), so a Title 41 reference there names a chapter, not a part, and matches no structural row here once the generation carries Title 41's compound parts (see the summary): match it at chapter level (`title = '41' AND part LIKE '60-%'`). NULL for ranges, publisher typos, unprefixed numbers (`Sec. 1-1`), parenthesized citations (`1.401(k)-1`), sections outside a numbered PART and section tokens the volume does not hold; 12 single sections printed with `§§` (`§§ 2.188`) are read as ranges until spicy-docs 0.31.0. For other granules, composed from the part and the identifier's tokens (e.g. `48-700`, `15-746.10-app1`); NULL without a part. A part-level reference (`40-60`) equals `cfr_ref` only on a part's structural rows, of which the part's own granule has `part_granule` `'true'`, and a part held only as sections has none (50 CFR 622 among 12 on 2026-10-03): match a part on `title` and `part`, which section rows carry. |
| `title` | `VARCHAR` | CFR title number from the package or granule identifier (e.g. `40`). |
| `part` | `VARCHAR` | For a section, the number in the enclosing PART heading of the package's annual volume XML (e.g. `1600`, `50-201`, `241`); NULL outside a numbered PART or when the volume does not hold the section. For a section's appendix or TOC (`sec746-10-app1`), its host section's part when the volume holds the host, else its token's leading number. For other granules, the identifier's part token including letter suffixes (e.g. `1203a`); in Title 41, whose identifiers cut a compound part at the hyphen, the compound part its part granule's heading states (`60-2`). |
| `section` | `VARCHAR` | For a section, the printed number less its `{part}.` prefix (e.g. `1` for § 50-201.1, `19-8.1` in Part 241, `1601.0-1` in Part 1600, `401(k)-1`). For a section's appendix or TOC, the rest of its token after the leading number (`10-app1`); for a section token the volume does not hold, the whole token. NULL for other granules. |
| `heading` | `VARCHAR` | Granule heading / caption text from GovInfo's list-level `title` field. |
| `structure_level` | `VARCHAR` | GovInfo granule class / structural level (e.g. `CONTENT`, `NODE`, `TOC`, `APPENDIX`). |
| `edition_year` | `VARCHAR` | Annual edition year from the package or granule identifier, falling back to the year in `dateIssued`. This is not necessarily the printed body revision year or proof of a substantive edition. |
| `last_modified` | `VARCHAR` | Granule `lastModified` when supplied, otherwise the enclosing package's `lastModified`. GovInfo's granule listing supplies none, so in practice every row carries its package's stamp. |
| `url` | `VARCHAR` | Canonical GovInfo details URL composed from the package and granule identifiers. |
| `part_granule` | `VARCHAR` | `'true'` on the granule that is a part itself (an id ending `-part200`, or `-part60-id334` in Title 41), `'false'` on every other row. A part's subparts, subject groups, appendices and table of contents share its `cfr_ref` and read `'false'`, so `part_granule = 'true'` picks the part out of them; a part citation's lookup does exactly that. Read from the granule id alone by SpicyDocs' grammar, never from the heading. A part held in two annual editions has one such row per edition, and a part printed across volumes one per volume (40 CFR part 60 spans volumes 7 to 9 of the 2025 edition). |
